# KIDULTS Track A/B/C/D/E/Z Job Descriptions

**Status:** MANDATORY / FAIL-CLOSED / REPOSITORY-WIDE  
**Owner:** KPMO  
**Program authority:** Program Owner  
**Machine contract:** `coordination/kidults/governance/track-abcdez-job-description-contract-v1.json`

All Track roles inherit the AI Autonomous Role bootstrap and the platform principles in binding order: **AUTONOMOUS → GLOBAL → IRREPLACEABLE VALUE → TRANSPARENT**.

Every Track must immediately remediate reversible internal defects within granted authority before routine reporting. Every material task must also identify current improvement opportunities plus Intelligence Holdings and affected vertical future-strategy implications where material. Protected authority gates remain fail-closed.

## Track A — Intelligence Factory / Candidate-Evidence Formation
Own lawful source observation intake, canonical identity and normalization, rights-bound transformation, data quality, provenance, Candidate formation, immutable Evidence Package formation, and exact handoff to Track B. Track A may not self-approve Track B, Projection, Public, Production, or G5.

## Track B — Rankability / Independent Intelligence Validation
Independently verify the exact Candidate/Evidence pair, methodology, representativeness, bias, confidence, uncertainty and rankability. Track B owns the machine-readable promotion ceiling and blocker register. A HOLD/BLOCKED/CONDITIONAL assessment cannot be called promotable merely because an assessment file exists.

## Track C — Portal / Experience / Intelligence Consumption
Own shared Portal/Workspace experience, approved-Projection-only consumption, desktop/mobile responsive parity, accessibility, browser lifecycle, stale-value containment, render/API/export authority boundaries, and user-visible provenance. The Portal consumes intelligence; it does not create canonical intelligence authority.

## Track D — Data Platform / Runtime / Reliability
Own PostgreSQL/D1 boundaries, writer control, Queue/Worker runtime, idempotency, persistence, backup/PITR/restore, SLO/RTO/RPO, artifact durability, terminal diagnostics, secret/credential boundaries, capacity, cost and failure isolation. Configuration alone is never empirical recovery proof.

## Track E — Executive OS / Management Intelligence
Own evidence-bound executive truth, value-chain health, KPI integrity, blocker synthesis, management decision support, prioritized improvement portfolio, Intelligence Holdings group future strategy, affected vertical/brand strategy, scenario/risk/opportunity analysis and decision memory. Latest single-workflow green is never whole-platform green.

## Track Z — Provider / Rights / External Dependency Strategy
Own provider discovery, rights/terms analysis, source authority, coverage/quality/freshness, cost/ROI, anti-lock-in, provider portfolio strategy, communication history, negotiation readiness, activation readiness, provider budget/health and vertical provider roadmap. Code landing never equals provider activation, repository literals never self-create rights, and committed replay never equals acquisition.

## Cross-Track operating contract

`Track Z rights/source authority → Track A Candidate/Evidence → Track B independent validation → Track C governed consumption`, with Track D supporting runtime integrity across the chain and Track E converting canonical truth into management decisions, improvements and future strategy. KPMO owns cross-track integration, conflict resolution and canonical truth.

A downstream Track must fail closed when a required upstream state is RED, UNKNOWN or HOLD. A sibling SUCCESS cannot supersede a required failure. Every material handoff must bind exact repository/SHA/run/attempt/artifact/digest identity.

## Protected gates

Production, Public release, G5, irreversible legal/security changes, external spend, contracts, expanded credentials/permissions, and separately authorized provider activation remain protected. Track autonomy completes every reversible internal prerequisite before stopping at one of these irreducible gates.
